sentences.text: Shri Vimal Kumar Gangwal, learned counsel for the appel  Shri Amit Rawal, learned G.A. for the respondent / Stat 1.

Heard on I.A. No.3310 of 2024, which is second (repeat) application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of remaining jail sentence and grant of bail on behalf of appellant No.2 Vesta S/o Dhulia.

2. Appellant has been convicted under Sections 498A, 304B and 201 of IPC and has been sentenced to undergo 3 years R.I. with fine of Rs.2,000/-, Life imprisonment and 3 years R.I. with fine of Rs.2,000/- respectively with usual default stipulation.

3. Brief facts of the case are that the marriage of deceased Rahbai @ Guddi was solemnized with the co-acuused-Madiya (son of present appellant), but after the marriage, she was subjected to cruelty for non-fulfilment of demand of dowry of motorcycle and goats.
On 06.05.2018 deceased informed her brother Maansingh on mobile phone that she was beaten by the co-accused Madiya for demand of dowry.
After sometime, dead body of the deceased was found lying near culvert in decomposed condition.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant is an innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this matter.
Present appellant is the father of co-accused-Madiya.
Deceased has committed suicide in Punjab and her dead body was found nearby her village.
Co-accused has given a sum of Rs.2,70,000/- to the father of the deceased as a dowry as a custom prevailed in tribal community, which was admitted by the father and brother of the deceased.
There is no direct evidence available on record to connect the present appellant with the aforementioned offence.
Cause of death was also suspicious.
Looking to old pendency of the cases for consideration, final conclusion of this appeal would take sufficient long time.
There is a strong case in favour of this appellant.
Hence, the execution of the remaining part of the jail sentence of the appellant be suspended till the final disposal of this appeal.

sentences.text: 4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State submits that I.A. No.16519 of 2023 which was an application for suspension of co-accused- Madiya has already been rejected by this Court vide order dated 05.02.2024, therefore, in these circumstances application for suspension of sentence of present appellant be also rejected.

5. In view of the above and keeping in view the fact that present appellant is the father-in-law of the deceased and there is no specific allegation against him I.A. No.3310 of 2024 is allowed and it stands closed.

It is directed that subject to deposit of fine amount with the trial Court, if not already deposited, and on furnishing personal bond by the appellant No.2-Vesta S/o Dhulia in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of learned trial Court, the custodial part of the jail sentence of the present appellant shall remain suspended till final disposal of this appeal.
The appellant, after being enlarged on bail shall mark his presence before the Registry of this Court on 29.07.2024 and on all such future dates as may be fixed in this behalf.
List the matter for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.

(VIVEK RUSIA) (ANIL VERMA)
 JUDGE JUDGE  Divyansh Madiya @ Kamru vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189751338/
